title: Canonical point-automorphism restriction and integral transport construction
statement: Fix a finite-field datum $D$ with algebraic closure $k$ and characteristic prime $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and let $g:s\to s$ be any scheme automorphism. Use the completed integral coefficient sheaf $\widehat R_s$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], its module category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and its derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\Gamma_R$ be evaluation at the terminal pro-etale object followed by restriction to the constant $R$-scalars, and let $R\Gamma_R$ be its exact termwise derived functor [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. Let $G_g$ be the exact module inverse image with the action transported by the specified coefficient isomorphism, and $P_g$ the completed integral derived pullback [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Define $\sigma_g:\Gamma_R\to\Gamma_R\circ G_g$ by the section-normalized restriction-and-coprojection transformation of [lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural] at integral coefficients, followed by the canonical unlift of constant scalars. Define $\sigma_g^D:R\Gamma_R\to R\Gamma_R\circ G_g^D$ by applying this transformation termwise, localizing at quasi-isomorphisms, and applying the canonical exact-functor composition comparison. For every derived $\widehat R_s$-module $K$, define $\kappa_{g,K}:G_g^D K\to P_g K$ by the specified chosen-resolution comparison of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], supplying its prime-unit witnesses from $\ell\ne p$. Define the point transport to be $t_{g,K}=R\Gamma_R(\kappa_{g,K})\circ\sigma^D_{g,K}$. These are the four existing constructions pointAutomorphismRestrictionModules, pointAutomorphismRestrictionDerived, pointTransportKappa, and pointTransport. No compatibility with scalar extension, constructibility assumption, or naturality assertion for the composite is part of this definition.
